questions.q: What relationship type correctly connects the Order Tracking Application to each of WEB-HARROW-01 and APP-HARROW-01?
options: Depends on :: Used by
Hosted on :: Hosts
Runs on :: Runs
No relationship is needed between an application and its servers
questions.explain: The application genuinely runs on each server, so "Runs on :: Runs" is the correct, accurate pair for both server relationships.

questions.q: Why does the application's relationship to Harrow Orders DB use "Depends on :: Used by" instead of "Runs on :: Runs"?
options: Because the application does not actually run on either server
Because the application doesn't run on the database — it depends on it for data, which is a different real relationship than running on a server
Because "Depends on" is the only relationship type that exists in cmdb_rel_type
Because database relationships are never modeled in cmdb_rel_ci
questions.explain: Picking the type that matches what's actually true matters — "Runs on" would misdescribe a data dependency as a hosting relationship.

questions.q: Opening the Dependency View on Harrow Orders DB instead of on the Order Tracking Application shows what, per this lab?
options: A completely different, unrelated set of relationship data
No relationships at all, since the database was built first
The same three underlying relationship records, read from the other side — a "Used by" relationship pointing back at the application
An error, because the Dependency View only works from the application's side
questions.explain: The Dependency View is a two-sided read of the same stored data — starting from either CI shows the same relationships, correctly reversed.

questions.q: What is the correct, complete impact statement for taking Harrow Orders DB offline for emergency maintenance?
options: A database server is going down, with no further effect worth noting
WEB-HARROW-01 and APP-HARROW-01 will go offline along with the database
The Order Tracking Application will be broken for the maintenance window, even though WEB-HARROW-01 and APP-HARROW-01 stay technically up and reachable
Nothing is affected, since the servers have no direct relationship to the database
questions.explain: The servers' own relationships to the application are "Runs on," not a database dependency — so they stay up, but the application they host is non-functional.

questions.q: Why does the impact-analysis chain in this lab legitimately stop at the Order Tracking Application rather than reaching a named business service?
options: Because business services can never be related to applications in ServiceNow
Because no CI representing the business service this application supports has been modeled yet — that's exactly the gap Chapter 3's Common Service Data Model is built to close
Because the lab made a modeling mistake that should be corrected immediately
Because business services are only visible through Discovery, not through relationships
questions.explain: The chain stops where the actual modeled data stops — accurately reflecting what's built so far, not a flaw to fix within this chapter.
